items.title: Ingrid Sertso interviewed by Monk Rowe, Woodstock, New York, August 11, 2014
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] I know there’s been a few instances of critics describing some of the free players, Archie Shepp and so forth, as sounding very angry.

ctx.x: Well it puts you more into music. The worse one side gets, the economy and politics and so on, government, the more musicians jump up. Because the more the need is there for creative expression. So the worse it gets the more we need to do music you know. In terms of effecting us, what’s happening in Iraq and Russia and so on, I don’t know. I wouldn’t know whether we would express that in the music. Probably unconsciously it would be woven in also. It’s not consciously otherwise it would be totally negative, no.
I know there’s been a few instances of critics describing some of the free players, Archie Shepp and so forth, as sounding very angry.
